def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energ:
## Definition

Let $V$ and $H$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $i:V\to H$ be an injective,
continuous linear map with dense range. Let $V^*$ be the continuous real linear
dual of $V$. Identify $H$ with its Hilbert dual by its inner product and embed
$H$ into $V^*$ by
$$h\longmapsto\bigl(v\longmapsto (h,i v)_H\bigr).$$
The resulting dense continuous embeddings are written
$$V\hookrightarrow H\cong H^*\hookrightarrow V^*$$
and $(V,H,V^*)$ is called an **evolution triple**. The pairing between $V^*$
and $V$ is denoted $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V^*,V}$.

For a Hilbert space $X$, $L^2(0,T;X)$ is the space of equivalence classes of
strongly measurable $X$-valued functions $w$ with
$$\int_0^T\|w(t)\|_X^2\,dt<\infty.$$
Strong measurability means being an almost-everywhere pointwise limit of
measurable simple functions. For $u\in L^2(0,T;V)$ and $g\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$,
say that $g$ is the **weak time derivative** of $u$ when
$$\int_0^T (i u(t),i v)_H\,\phi'(t)\,dt =-\int_0^T\langle g(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\,\phi(t)\,dt$$
for every $v\in V$ and every $\phi\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$. The derivative is
unique up to equality almost everywhere. The **parabolic energy space** is
$$W(0,T;V):=\{u\in L^2(0,T;V):u'\in L^2(0,T;V^*)\},$$
with norm
$$\|u\|_{W(0,T;V)}:=\bigl(\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}^2+ \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;V^*)}^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$
No endpoint values are part of this definition; they are assigned only after
a continuous $H$ trace representative has been proved. Separability is an
additional hypothesis when it is needed by a later result.
lem-parabolic-bochner-l2-approximate-ide:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space, let
$q\in L^2(\mathbb R;X)$ be strongly measurable, and let $(\eta_\epsilon)$ be
a nonnegative smooth mollifier family of mass one. Define
$$q_\epsilon(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\eta_\epsilon(t-s)q(s)\,ds.$$
Then each $q_\epsilon$ is smooth with values in $X$ and
$$\|q_\epsilon-q\|_{L^2(\mathbb R;X)}\longrightarrow0\qquad(\epsilon\downarrow0).$$
lem-parabolic-discrete-energy-identity:
## Statement

For every real Hilbert space $H$ and $x,y\in H$,
$$2(x-y,x)_H=\|x\|_H^2-\|y\|_H^2+\|x-y\|_H^2.$$
lem-parabolic-hilbert-bnb-criterion:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces and let
$b:X\times Y\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded bilinear form. Suppose there is
$\beta>0$ such that
$$\sup_{\|y\|_Y\le1}|b(x,y)|\ge\beta\|x\|_X\qquad(x\in X),$$
and the only $y\in Y$ satisfying $b(x,y)=0$ for every $x\in X$ is $y=0$.
Then, for every bounded linear functional $F:Y\to\mathbb R$, there is a
unique $x\in X$ such that $b(x,y)=F(y)$ for every $y\in Y$, and
$$\|x\|_X\le\beta^{-1}\|F\|_{Y^*},\qquad \|F\|_{Y^*}:=\sup_{\|y\|_Y\le1}|F(y)|.$$
alg-parabolic-backward-euler-averaged-fo:
## Definition

Input a finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V_h\subset V$ with its
inherited $H$ inner product and $V$ norm; a finite-element use instantiates it
with a zero-boundary conforming polynomial space. Input also a final time
$T>0$, a finite partition
$0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$, a measurable family of bounded coercive
forms $a(t;\cdot,\cdot)$, $f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$, and an initial value
$U^0\in V_h$. For
$I_j=(t_{j-1},t_j)$ and $\tau_j=t_j-t_{j-1}$, form scalar averages
$$\bar a_j(v,w)=\tau_j^{-1}\int_{I_j}a(t;v,w)\,dt,\qquad \bar f_j=\tau_j^{-1}\int_{I_j}f(t)\,dt.$$
For $j=1,\ldots,N$, solve for $U^j\in V_h$ from
$$\tau_j^{-1}(U^j-U^{j-1},v_h)_H+ \bar a_j(U^j,v_h)=\langle\bar f_j,v_h\rangle_{V^*,V} \qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$
Return the nodes $U^0,\ldots,U^N$, the piecewise-constant function
$\bar U(t)=U^j$ on each open interval $(t_{j-1},t_j)$ (endpoint values do
not affect the $L^2$ function), and the continuous piecewise
affine reconstruction $\widehat U$ joining consecutive nodes. The initial
value is the separately supplied $U^0$; the initial jump is
$U^1-U^0$, and subsequent jumps are $U^j-U^{j-1}$. Invalid spaces, partitions,
or form/data hypotheses return `invalid-input`; the well-definedness theorem
proves that each indicated solve has a unique answer under the stated
hypotheses. Because coefficients and loads are averaged,
this procedure is defined on their almost-everywhere equivalence classes and
does not sample a representative at a point. For a time-dependent form this
is the averaged-coefficient backward Euler method; with piecewise-constant
time trials it is also the $dG(0)$ step.
alg-parabolic-crank-nicolson-cg1:
## Definition

Input a finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V_h\subset V$ with its
inherited $H$ inner product and $V$ norm; a finite-element use instantiates it
with a zero-boundary conforming polynomial space. Input also a final time
$T>0$, a finite partition
$0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, a time-independent real bounded coercive
bilinear form $a$ on $V$, a load $f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$, and $U^0\in V_h$.
Put $\bar f_j=\tau_j^{-1}\int_{t_{j-1}}^{t_j}f(t)\,dt$. For
$j=1,\ldots,N$, solve
$$\tau_j^{-1}(U^j-U^{j-1},v_h)_H+ a\!\left(\frac{U^j+U^{j-1}}2,v_h\right) =\langle\bar f_j,v_h\rangle\qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$
Return the nodal values and their continuous piecewise-linear interpolant.
There are no interior time jumps; the initial value is the supplied $U^0$.
The coefficient form is time-independent, while the load is averaged, so no
point value of an $L^2(V^*)$ equivalence class is used. Invalid inputs return
`invalid-input`; the well-definedness theorem proves that each indicated step
has a unique solution under the stated hypotheses.

For each interval, the same equation is the continuous-Galerkin $cG(1)$
equation with continuous piecewise-linear trial functions and constant test
functions: integrating $U'$ gives $U^j-U^{j-1}$, and integrating the linear
trial function in the time-independent form gives its midpoint value. Thus
this item asserts the $cG(1)$ equivalence only; it does not assert rates for
higher-degree $cG$ or discontinuous-Galerkin methods.
lem-parabolic-bochner-time-mollification:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(V,H,V^*)$ be a real evolution triple and
$u\in W(0,T;V)$. There are smooth $V$-valued functions $u_n$ on a
neighborhood of $[0,T]$ such that
$$u_n\to u\quad\hbox{in }L^2(0,T;V),\qquad u_n'\to u'\quad\hbox{in }L^2(0,T;V^*).$$
The weak time derivative in the definition of $W(0,T;V)$ is unique up to
almost-everywhere equality. No separability assumption on $V$ is needed.
lem-parabolic-measurable-form-operators-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a separable real Hilbert space, let $T>0$, and let
$q\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$. Suppose $a(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ is real bilinear and
$t\mapsto a(t;v,w)$ is measurable for each fixed $v,w\in V$. Assume there
is one null set outside which
$$|a(t;v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad a(t;v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2$$
for all $v,w\in V$, with $M<\infty$ and $\alpha>0$. For a.e. $t$ outside
that null set define $A(t)v\in V^*$ and $A^*(t)v\in V^*$ by
$$\langle A(t)v,w\rangle=a(t;v,w),\qquad \langle A^*(t)v,w\rangle=a(t;w,v).$$
Then, for every $u\in L^2(0,T;V)$, both $t\mapsto A(t)u(t)$ and
$t\mapsto A^*(t)u(t)$ are strongly measurable and belong to
$L^2(0,T;V^*)$. For a.e. $t$, the two equations
$$a(t;x(t),v)=\langle q(t),v\rangle,\qquad a(t;v,x^*(t))=\langle q(t),v\rangle\qquad(v\in V)$$
have unique solutions. The solution functions $x,x^*$ are strongly
measurable, belong to $L^2(0,T;V)$, and satisfy
$$\|x(t)\|_V,\ \|x^*(t)\|_V\le\alpha^{-1}\|q(t)\|_{V^*}\quad\text{a.e.}$$
On the exceptional null set set all operator actions and solutions to zero.
lem-parabolic-projection-time-product-ru:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a separable real Hilbert space and $Y$ a real Hilbert space, and
let $u\in H^1(0,T;X)$ (meaning
$u,u'\in L^2(0,T;X)$ with distribution derivative). It has a unique
continuous representative on $[0,T]$. Let
$P\in\mathcal L(X,Y)$ be a fixed bounded linear map. Then
$Pu\in H^1(0,T;Y)$ and $(Pu)'=Pu'$.

If instead $P:[0,T]\to\mathcal L(X,Y)$ is continuously differentiable in
operator norm, then $P(t)u(t)\in H^1(0,T;Y)$ and
$$\frac{d}{dt}(P(t)u(t))=P'(t)u(t)+P(t)u'(t)\quad\text{a.e.}$$
In particular, a differentiable time-dependent Ritz comparison contributes
the term $P'(t)u(t)$ to its residual derivative.
lem-parabolic-weak-compactness-separable:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Every bounded sequence in a separable real Hilbert
space $X$ has a weakly convergent subsequence. If $V$ is a separable real
Hilbert space, then $L^2(0,T;V)$ and $L^2(0,T;V^*)$ are separable real Hilbert
spaces, their product is a separable Hilbert space, and the graph of the weak
time-derivative operator is closed there. Consequently $W(0,T;V)$ is a closed
Hilbert subspace of that product and every bounded sequence in $W(0,T;V)$ has
a weakly convergent subsequence.
lem-parabolic-zero-boundary-sobolev-spac:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded
polyhedral open set with $d\ge1$. Put
$$H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R),\qquad V=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R),\qquad \|v\|_V=\|v\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}.$$
Then $V$ is a separable real Hilbert space, and the inclusion
$V\hookrightarrow H$ is continuous, injective and dense. Consequently
$(V,H,V^*)$ is a real evolution triple in the sense of
[[def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energy-space]]. The gradient norm
$\|\nabla v\|_{L^2}$ is equivalent to this norm on $V$ by Poincare's
inequality.
thm-parabolic-finite-dimensional-measura:
## Statement

Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional real subspace of an evolution space $V$,
continuously included in $H$. Let $a(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ be real bilinear,
measurable in $t$, uniformly bounded by $M$ and coercive by $\alpha>0$ on
$V_h$. If $f\in L^2(0,T;V_h^*)$ and $u_h^0\in V_h$, then there is a unique
$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ with $u_h(0)=u_h^0$ and
$$((u_h)'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;u_h(t),v_h)=\langle f(t),v_h\rangle$$
for every $v_h\in V_h$ and almost every $t$. It satisfies
$$\|u_h(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u_h(s)\|_V^2\,ds \le \|u_h^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V_h^*}^2\,ds.$$
Here $H^1(0,T;V_h)$ means absolutely continuous $V_h$-valued coefficient
functions whose value and derivative are square-integrable.
def-parabolic-ritz-projection:
## Definition

Let $(V,H,V^*)$ be a real evolution triple and let $V_h\subset V$ be a
finite-dimensional conforming subspace. In a mesh instance, the algebraic
piecewise-polynomial conventions are those of
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]; the required inclusion into
$V$ is an explicit hypothesis of this definition. Let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be time-independent,
bounded, and coercive as in
[[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]], with constants
$M$ and $\alpha>0$. For $u\in V$, the equation for the unknown $z_h\in V_h$
$$a(z_h,v_h)=a(u,v_h)\qquad\text{for every }v_h\in V_h$$
is the **Ritz equation**; any solution $z_h$ is called a Ritz projection of
$u$. The item [[lem-parabolic-ritz-projection-well-defined]] proves that for
every $u$ there is exactly one solution, denoted $R_hu$, and that these
solutions define a bounded linear map $R_h:V\to V_h$. The form need not be
symmetric.
lem-parabolic-energy-pairing-and-trace:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(V,H,V^*)$ be the real evolution triple of
[[def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energy-space]], and let
$u,v\in W(0,T;V)$. Each has a unique representative in $C([0,T];H)$, and
for all $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2-\|u(s)\|_H^2 =2\int_s^t\langle u'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\,dr,$$
$$(u(t),v(t))_H-(u(s),v(s))_H =\int_s^t\bigl(\langle u'(r),v(r)\rangle_{V^*,V} +\langle v'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\bigr)\,dr.$$
Writing $c_i=\|i:V\to H\|$, the trace obeys
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|u(t)\|_H^2 \le \frac{c_i^2}{T}\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}^2 +2\|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;V^*)}\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}.$$
thm-parabolic-backward-euler-error-and-r:
## Statement

Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional conforming subspace of a real evolution
triple, let $a(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ be scalar measurable and uniformly bounded by
$M$ and coercive by $\alpha>0$, and let $f\in L^2(0,T;V_h^*)$. Let
$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ be the semidiscrete solution from
[[thm-parabolic-finite-dimensional-measurable-ode]]. On a finite partition
$0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, put $\tau_j=t_j-t_{j-1}$ and
$\tau_{\max}=\max_j\tau_j$. For the interval-averaged backward Euler values
$U^j$ from [[alg-parabolic-backward-euler-averaged-forms]], define
$e^j=U^j-u_h(t_j)$ and let $\widehat U$ be the affine reconstruction, with
$\overline U(t)=U^j$ on $(t_{j-1},t_j)$. Every step has a unique solution.
With
$$C_U=\|U^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|f\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2,$$
the separate maximum and cumulative bounds are
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|U^m\|_H^2\le C_U,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^N\|U^j-U^{j-1}\|_H^2+ \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|U^j\|_V^2\le C_U.$$
The reconstruction satisfies
$$\|\widehat U'\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2 \le2\|f\|_{L^2(V_h^*)}^2+2M^2\|\overline U\|_{L^2(V)}^2,$$
$$\|\widehat U-\overline U\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2 \le\frac{c_i^2\tau_{\max}}3 \sum_{j=1}^N\|U^j-U^{j-1}\|_H^2,$$
where $c_i=\|V\hookrightarrow H\|$. For the nodal error, define
$$C_e=\|e^0\|_H^2+ \frac{M^2}{\alpha}\tau_{\max}^2 \|u_h'\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h)}^2.$$
Then the error obeys the separate bounds
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|e^m\|_H^2\le C_e,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|e^j\|_V^2\le C_e.$$
Thus exact initial projection $U^0=u_h(0)$ gives first-order maximum nodal
error. The reconstruction estimates provide bounds for later compactness
arguments; they do not themselves assert compactness.
thm-parabolic-crank-nicolson-second-orde:
## Statement

Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional conforming subspace of a real evolution
triple. Assume a time-independent real bilinear form $a$ is bounded by $M$
and coercive by $\alpha>0$, the load $f\in L^2(0,T;V_h^*)$, and the
partition and data of [[alg-parabolic-crank-nicolson-cg1]]. Every time step
has a unique solution and, with
$U^{\mathrm{mid},j}=(U^j+U^{j-1})/2$,
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|U^m\|_H^2\le C_U,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|U^{\mathrm{mid},j}\|_V^2\le C_U, \quad C_U:=\|U^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|f\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2.$$
If the exact semidiscrete solution $u_h$ from
[[thm-parabolic-finite-dimensional-measurable-ode]] satisfies
$u_h\in H^2(0,T;V_h)$, meaning $u_h,u_h',u_h''\in L^2(0,T;V_h)$ with weak
time derivatives. Under this regularity assumption, set
$e^j=U^j-u_h(t_j)$, $\tau_{\max}=\max_j\tau_j$, and
$$C_e:=\|e^0\|_H^2+ \frac{M^2}{16\alpha}\tau_{\max}^4 \|u_h''\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h)}^2.$$
Then the error satisfies the separate bounds
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|e^m\|_H^2\le C_e,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j \left\|\frac{e^j+e^{j-1}}2\right\|_V^2\le C_e.$$
Thus exact initial projection $U^0=u_h(0)$ gives second-order maximum nodal
error. The regularity hypothesis is on the time-dependent semidiscrete
solution and is not implied by the method definition.
lem-parabolic-ritz-projection-well-defin:
## Statement

Let $V_h\subset V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $a$ be a real bounded
coercive bilinear form with constants $M$ and $\alpha>0$. For every $u\in V$
there is a unique $R_hu\in V_h$ satisfying the defining equation of
[[def-parabolic-ritz-projection]]. The map $R_h:V\to V_h$ is linear and
$$\|R_hu\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\|u\|_V.$$
The argument uses only finite-dimensional linear algebra; it adds no choice
axiom.
thm-parabolic-variational-wellposedness-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $T>0$, let $V$ be a separable real Hilbert
space, and let $(V,H,V^*)$ be its real evolution triple. Suppose
$a(t;\cdot,\cdot):V\times V\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and scalar measurable
for each fixed pair $v,w\in V$, and there is one null set outside which
$$|a(t;v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad a(t;v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2$$
for all $v,w\in V$, with constants $M>0$ and $\alpha>0$. Let
$f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$ and $u_0\in H$. Then there is a unique
$u\in W(0,T;V)$ with $u(0)=u_0$ and, for almost every $t$,
$$\langle u'(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}+a(t;u(t),v) =\langle f(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\qquad(v\in V).$$
For every $t\in[0,T]$ it satisfies
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u(s)\|_V^2\,ds \le\|u_0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V^*}^2\,ds.$$
The proof applies BNB to the space-time form. Scalar measurability suffices
because $V$ is separable and the measurable inverse action is proved locally.
thm-parabolic-fem-semidiscrete-existence:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded
polyhedral open set, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine
simplicial mesh of $\Omega$, and choose $k\in\mathbb N_0$. Let
$V=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with its $W^{1,2}$ norm,
$H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and let $V^*$ be the continuous dual of $V$;
these spaces form the separable real evolution triple proved in
[[lem-parabolic-zero-boundary-sobolev-space-is-separable]]. Let $V_h$ be the
scalar degree-at-most-$k$ conforming polynomial subspace on $\mathcal T_h$
whose polynomial traces vanish on every boundary facet, as defined by
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Suppose the real bilinear
form $a(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ on $V$ is scalar measurable and there is one null
set outside which it is bounded by $M$ and coercive by $\alpha>0$ on $V$.
Let $f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$ and $u_h^0\in V_h$. Then there is a unique
$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ with $u_h(0)=u_h^0$ satisfying
$$((u_h)'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;u_h(t),v_h)=\langle f(t),v_h\rangle_{V^*,V} \qquad(v_h\in V_h)$$
for almost every $t$. For every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|u_h(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u_h(s)\|_V^2\,ds \le\|u_h^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V^*}^2\,ds.$$
thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-sp:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the bounded polyhedral mesh setting, spaces,
form and data of [[thm-parabolic-fem-semidiscrete-existence-energy]]. Let $u$
be the continuous solution supplied by
[[thm-parabolic-variational-wellposedness-and-energy-stability]] on the same
evolution triple and let $u_h$ be the corresponding semidiscrete solution.
For this error identity, assume the additional regularity $u\in H^1(0,T;V)$,
meaning $u,u'\in L^2(0,T;V)$ with the unique continuous representative
supplied by [[lem-parabolic-projection-time-product-rule]]. Let
$P_h:V\to V_h$ be a fixed bounded linear
comparison map, define
$$\rho(t)=P_hu(t)-u(t),\qquad\theta(t)=u_h(t)-P_hu(t),$$
and let $\mathcal R_h(t)\in V_h^*$ be the full residual
$$\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h)=(\rho'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\rho(t),v_h).$$
Then for almost every $t$ and every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$(\theta'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\theta(t),v_h)=-\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h),$$
and for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|\theta(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|\theta(s)\|_V^2ds \le\|\theta(0)\|_H^2+ \alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|\mathcal R_h(s)\|_{V_h^*}^2ds.$$

The same identity and energy bound hold for an operator-norm $C^1$
time-dependent comparison map $P_h(t):V\to V_h$, with its time derivative
included in $\rho'$ as stated below. For a time-independent form and the
Ritz projection $P_h=R_h$ from
[[def-parabolic-ritz-projection]], Galerkin orthogonality makes
$a(\rho(t),v_h)=0$, so the residual is exactly
$(R_hu'(t)-u'(t),v_h)_H$. If a time-dependent comparison $P_h(t)$ is used,
it must be operator-norm $C^1$; then
$\rho'=P_h'(t)u+P_h(t)u'-u'$, including the projection-derivative term.
For a measurable time-dependent form with a fixed comparison map, no
orthogonality is inferred and the full displayed residual remains.
cor-parabolic-semidiscrete-spatial-error:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the real scalar finite-element setting of
[[cor-shape-regular-affine-fe-primal-energy-approximation]], on a
shape-regular affine mesh family with $h\le1$. Let $V=H^1_0(\Omega)$
with its $H^1$ norm,
$H=L^2(\Omega)$, and let $a$ be a time-independent bounded coercive form
with constants $M,\alpha$. Let $R_h$ be its Ritz projection and let $u_h$
be the semidiscrete solution initialized by $u_h(0)=R_hu(0)$. Assume the
continuous solution obeys $u\in H^1(0,T;V)$,
$$u\in L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap V),\qquad u'\in L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap V),$$
for an integer $r\ge1$. For almost every $t$, assume the adjoint solution
and approximation inequalities in
[[cor-aubin-nitsche-h-r-plus-s-rate-under-primal-and-dual-approximation]]
hold for each target $w=u(t)$ and $w=u'(t)$ with common
$s\in(0,1]$, $C_D$, and $C_R$, uniformly in $h,t$. Let $C_{\rm FE}$ be the
primal interpolation constant in that corollary and put
$$C_A=\frac{M^2}{\alpha}C_{\rm FE}C_DC_R, \qquad c_i=\|V\hookrightarrow H\|.$$
Then $\rho=R_hu-u$ and $\theta=u_h-R_hu$ satisfy
$$\|\rho\|_{L^\infty(0,T;V)} \le\frac M\alpha C_{\rm FE}h^r \|u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},$$
$$\|\rho\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)} \le C_Ah^{r+s}\|u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},\qquad \|\rho'\|_{L^2(0,T;H)} \le C_Ah^{r+s}\|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},$$
and
$$\|\theta\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)} \le\frac{c_i C_A}{\sqrt\alpha}h^{r+s} \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},\qquad \|\theta\|_{L^2(0,T;V)} \le\frac{c_i C_A}{\alpha}h^{r+s} \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})}.$$
Consequently, $\|u_h-u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)}$ is bounded by the sum of the two
$L^\infty(0,T;H)$ bounds for $\rho,\theta$, and
$$\|u_h-u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)} \le\sqrt T\frac M\alpha C_{\rm FE}h^r \|u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2})} +\frac{c_i C_A}{\alpha}h^{r+s} \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})}.$$
In particular, the full-adjoint branch $s=1$ gives the conditional
semidiscrete max-in-time rate $h^{r+1}$ in $L^\infty(H)$; it requires both stated dual hypotheses and
does not assert full adjoint regularity on an arbitrary polyhedral domain.
